objects.original: Actual sphere marginal laws rho_t=(X_t)#P, test expectation F and generator average G.
objects.reconstructed: Put d=card(I), c=real(max(d-1,0)) (natural-number subtraction before casting), E=R^I with Euclidean norm, S={x in E: ||x||=1}, V_j(x)=e_j-x_j*x, and L_S f(x)=Laplacian(f)(x)-D^2 f(x)[x,x]-c*Df(x)[x]. Here Df is the Frechet derivative and D^2 f=D(Df). Write R_+=[0,infinity), and let lambda_T be Lebesgue measure on [0,T], transported to R_+ (the given comap of volume restricted to [0,T]). All time integrals below use this measure unless indicated otherwise. A ProgressiveL2Integrand eta on horizon T is a real process eta(t,omega), strongly progressive for the filtration, with (omega,t) -> eta(t,omega) in L^2(P x lambda_T). I_T^j(eta) denotes the supplied completed continuous Ito process driven by the scalar coordinate B_j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j: the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic-integral approximations off their null uniform-Cauchy bad set, zero on that bad set, and held constant after T; at each t<=T it agrees almost everywhere with the L^2-completion integral up to t. Let rho(t)=(X(t,.))_*P be the law on S obtained by mapping P under X(t,.). Put F(r)=integral_S f(w)d rho(max(r,0)) and G(r)=integral_S [-Df(w)[u(max(r,0),w)]+a(max(r,0))*L_S f(w)]d rho(max(r,0)). The integrand's toLp operation is its L^2 equivalence class represented by (omega,t)->eta(t,omega).

assumptions.original: Jointly measurable sphere X; continuous field; Borel nonnegative temperature locally pointwise bounded; usual Brownian setup; ambient C² test and simultaneous horizon equations.
assumptions.reconstructed: The vector Brownian hypothesis means B(0,omega)=0 for every omega; increments on finite families of pairwise disjoint half-open intervals are jointly independent; every continuous real linear functional ell sends B(t)-B(s), s<t, to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||^2; paths are P-almost surely continuous. B is strongly adapted, and for every s<=t the increment B(t)-B(s) is independent of the sigma-algebra filtration(s). The filtration is right continuous, and every P-null subset of Omega belongs to filtration(t) for every t>=0 (completeness at each time). X is jointly measurable. u is jointly continuous. Temperature a is measurable, everywhere nonnegative, and for each T>=0 there is a real C_T with |a(t)|<=C_T for all t<=T. For every T>0 there exist eta_ij in ProgressiveL2Integrand(filtration,P,T), x:Omega->R^I and b_i:R_+ x Omega->R such that each x_i is strongly measurable with respect to filtration(0), each b_i is strongly progressive, each b_i(.,omega) is lambda_T-integrable for P-a.e. omega, and the following three pathwise identities hold P-a.e., each uniformly for t<=T: X_i(t)=x_i+integral_0^t b_i(v)dv+sum_j I_T^j(eta_ij)(t); b(t)=-u(t,X(t))-a(t)*c*X(t); for every j, (eta_ij(t))_i=sqrt(2*a(t))*V_j(X(t)). f is C^2 at every point of S. No separate progressive or continuous-path assumption on X is listed.

conclusion.original: G locally integrable on R; oriented F(b)-F(a)=integral_a^b G; AC on every [0,T]; F'=G a.e. on (0,infinity).
